Non-native English speaker here, can you explain why?

It's pretty logical really. When you speak about a group of people you put the others first and yourself last (hey, it's only polite!). To check whether it should be "I" or "me" you remove the other people from the sentence and then it should follow the normal grammatical rules for whatever you were saying.

For example:
Sarah and I are going to the cinema
Sarah and me are going to the cinema

I am going to the cinema
Me is going to the cinema

In this case "I" is correct because Sarah and I are the subject of the sentence, the cinema is the object. I am doing the action in this sentence.

Sarah is taking a picture of my parents and me
Sarah is taking a picture of my parents and I

Sarah is taking a picture of me
Sarah is taking a picture of I

In this case "my parents and me" is the object of the sentence- we are having the action done to us- and therefore it is "me" rather than "I", since only "I" does actions.
